**STEP 1 - Scene:** A small side dish of blanched or steamed broccoli florets with sliced cucumber and dark, glossy strands of seaweed or wood-ear fungus. It is photographed from above, on a white square plate sitting on a paper placemat with QR codes. Food is only in the upper-middle part of the plate.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white square plate is about 20 cm across, so its area is about 400 cm². The plate is the vessel.

**STEP 3 - Items:** (1) broccoli florets, (2) cucumber slices, (3) dark seaweed or wood-ear fungus. No dressing or oil is clearly visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Broccoli about 12% (48 cm²), cucumber about 5% (20 cm²), dark fungus about 3% (12 cm²). Total food coverage is about 20% of the plate, which matches the sparse pile.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Broccoli 48 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 144 ml. Cucumber 20 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 30 ml. Fungus 12 cm² × 0.5 cm ≈ 6 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Broccoli 144 ml × 0.5 ≈ 72 g. Cucumber 30 ml × 0.6 ≈ 18 g. Fungus 6 ml × 0.3 ≈ 2 g, rounded up to about 4 g because the strands are thin and may be hidden.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Broccoli (cooked) 72 g × 35 kcal/100 g ≈ 25 kcal. Cucumber 18 g × 15 kcal/100 g ≈ 3 kcal. Fungus 4 g × 30 kcal/100 g ≈ 1 kcal. Total ≈ 29 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 94 g of lightly cooked vegetables and fungus on a sparse plate is plausible. Energy is low, as expected for non-starchy vegetables with no visible oil or dressing.
